new_statements.quote: In Western Popoloca (Williams and E. Pike 1968: 379), the stressed syllable usually, but not always, coincides with the end of the grammatical stem. In Northern Popoloca (Stark 1976), tone is contrastive in stems; stem tones may override prefix tones. Kalstrom and E. Pike (1968) discuss stress in Eastern Popoloca. The penultimate vowel of the stem (the nucleus of the phonological word) receives stress, with the stressed component being long, either by consonant lengthening or vowel lengthening.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: opened (author-hosted De Gruyter page proofs, 64 pp.). PDF page 19 carries the running footer '(p. 267)'; layout lines 37-39 read exactly: 'In Western Popoloca (Williams and E. Pike 1968: 379), the stressed syllable usually, but not always, coincides with the end of the grammatical stem.' The remainder of the recorded quote (Northern Popoloca / Stark 1976; Kalstrom & E. Pike 1968 on Eastern Popoloca, 'The penultimate vowel of the stem (the nucleus of the phonological word) receives stress, with the stressed component being long...') continues verbatim across p. 267 line 39 to p. 268 lines 1-2 (also lines 1151-1160). The chapter's reference list (txt line 4145) gives 'Williams,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: One primary stress per word, located with reference to morphology: it normally falls on the last syllable of the grammatical stem (so suffixes/enclitics follow the stress), but the source notes the match is 'usually, but not always', i.e. some words have stress off the stem-final syllable. Could alternatively be coded fixed-final with domain = stem; the primary (Williams & Pike 1968: 379) must be read to decide and to learn how the exceptions behave.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in the second-hand report.
new_statements.exceptions: 'usually, but not always' coincides with the end of the stem — exceptions exist but are not characterised in the survey.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the grammatical stem within the word (three-tone language; tone is contrastive independently of stress). Statement is a survey paraphrase, not the primary description; the primary Lingua article could not be opened from our machine.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the Popoloca of San Felipe Otlaltepec, Puebla (= 'Western Popoloca' in SIL usage; ISO pow, Glottolog sanf1264). Williams & Pike 1968 and Pierson 1952 are explicitly catalogued by SIL as descriptions of 'Western (Otlaltepec) Popoloca'. Do not conflate with Eastern (San Juan Atzingo, poe), Northern (Tlacoyalco, pls), Metzontla (pbe) or Temalacayuca (pps) Popoloca, whose stress descriptions (penultimate / variable) differ.
